newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares ends off in weak profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares ends off in weak profit taking.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange slipped in profit taking but showed signs of having reached support levels, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 0.50 percent to 9,216.98, as 27 stocks fell, eight rose and 10 closed flat.
Strong profit taking early in the session was replaced by buying towards the close as brokers investors took heart in the rebound of the Brazilian market, brokers said.
Judging by demand for stocks at the end of trading, prices should rise towards the end of the week, they said.
"Even though the market started off with clear tendency to fall it rebounded to close as we saw," said Mario Simosa of the Multinvest brokerage.
Total trade was 5.995 billion bolivars ($12.23 million).

Among leading stocks, bellwether Electricidad de Caracas rose 4.00 bolivars to 806.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV rose 25.00 bolivars to 3,025.00 bolivars, while cement company Vencemos class 1 stock fell 10.00 bolivars to 1049.00 bolivars and class 2 stock fell 10.00 bolivars to 940.00 bolivars.
